description_full: SBA Communications Corporation is a leading independent owner and operator of wireless communications infrastructure, including tower structures, rooftops and other structures that support antennas used for wireless communications. In our site leasing business, we lease space to wireless service providers and other customers on assets we own or operate, and manage rooftop and tower sites for property owners under various contractual arrangements. As of December 31, 2025, we owned 46,328 towers, a substantial portion of which were built by us or by other tower owners or operators who, like us, build towers to lease space to multiple wireless service providers. As of December 31, 2025, each of our towers had an average of 1.8 tenants. SBA Communications Corporation was established in 1989 and was incorporated in Florida.
ceo_bio: Mr. Brendan Thomas Cavanagh CPA | CEO, President & Director | Age 53 | Compensation: $2.7M (FY2025)
culture_narrative: Employs approximately 1K people. Revenue per employee of $1.5M ranks in the below the sector median among Real Estate peers, with revenue growing 11%/yr across its filed history. Each employee generates $578K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $41K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 2× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags moderate compensation governance risk (4/10).
financial_summary: SBA Communications Corporation is a large-cap real estate business with a $19.8B market cap on $2.8B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +2% over the past three years and +6% annually across the full decade, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory. Operating margins are expanding by +2.4pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.

Returns on capital run at 12% against a 7% cost of capital, a 5-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it. Gross margins of 75% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $1.1B in free cash flow — roughly 38 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.23× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 7.7× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 2.9× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 4.9% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 2.4× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

sect: Its 48% operating margin runs 25pp above the Real Estate median (23%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It captures 2.41x its revenue share in sector profits, taking a disproportionate slice of the profit pool.
It accounts for 0.8% of sector revenue and 1.9% of sector operating profit.
Over five years it has been gaining share of the sector profit pool (+3.0% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 146 companies in the universe; the top four hold 25% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are roughly flat over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 16% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 36% and a beta of 0.77, it is more defensive than the market, though its beta has shifted (1y 0.83 vs 5y 0.70), so read it loosely.
Liquidity is deep, with about $161.1M traded a day.
In past sell-offs it fell 29% in the 2020 crash, 36% in the 2022 bear market and 72% in 2008.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $153 (margin of safety -24%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 23%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $103 to $225 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
Against its own history it is cheap: the EBIT multiple sits 50% below its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 5.4% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 3.9% (vs the 8% bar).
The 20 covering analysts target $223 on average, 18% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
The price implies 4.7% annual cash-flow growth.
prof: ROIC of 12% earns above the cost of capital of 7.0%, but the 5pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.61).
It runs a 75% gross margin and converts 38% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 7/9 and cash conversion of 1.23x.
AFFO margin (a proxy for distributable REIT cash) is 38%.
Operating margin is running 13pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
It spends 2.7% of revenue on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: Leverage is heavy at 7.7x net debt to EBITDA ($271.2M of cash against $12.9B of debt), and interest cover is thin at 2.9x.
Warning signs: an Altman Z of 0.27 in the distress zone.
The current ratio of 0.29 means short-term liabilities exceed current assets.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 2.2% over 3 years, 6.2% over 5 years and 5.6% over 10 years, so growth is decelerating.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Free cash flow has compounded 1.3% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
Forward indicators: deferred revenue up 36% and FFO growth of 2.8% a year over five years.
Capex runs only 0.8x depreciation (8.0% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.8%), and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
It returns 4.9% a year to shareholders (2.5% in buybacks and 2.6% in dividends).
The share count has shrunk 0.8% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
people: With about 1,844 employees, each generates about $1.5M of revenue, 0.7x the Real Estate median, and revenue has grown 10.5% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $578K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $2.7M (2x revenue per employee).
